HR Recovery Guidelines
💚
Good recovery: HR drops 20+ bpm in the first minute after stopping
💛
Average recovery: HR drops 12–20 bpm in the first minute
❤️
Poor recovery: HR drops less than 12 bpm — may indicate overtraining or low fitness
You can log your 1-minute post-activity HR when adding HR data to an activity. This enables more accurate recovery tracking.

Help Guides 1 / 9
Dashboard — Your Command Center
The Dashboard shows your Year-to-Date totals for running, walking, cycling, and steps across the top cards. Below that, you'll find your activity streak, a calendar heatmap colour-coded by effort, and interactive charts that break down your training over time.

All numbers update live the moment you log a new activity — no refresh needed.
Click any chart legend item to toggle that data series on or off.
My Races — Plan & Track Events
Add upcoming races with a date, distance, type, goal time, and notes. Each race card shows key details at a glance. Tap a card to edit any field or delete the race entirely.

Completed races are archived automatically once the date passes, so you can revisit your race history any time.
Use the location and elevation fields to better prepare for hilly or trail races.
Pace Editor — Fine-Tune Your Targets
The floating Pace Editor widget (bottom-left on the Dashboard) lets you set custom target paces for Easy, Medium, and Hard effort levels.

Type a pace like 5:30 and it saves automatically. All pace recommendations, coach cards, and race predictions re-render instantly across every section — no reload required.
The widget is draggable — grab the header to move it anywhere on screen. Click the minimize button to collapse it.
Heart Rate — Train by Zones
The Heart Rate section lets you define your max heart rate and view training split across four effort zones. Each zone targets a different physiological adaptation:

Easy (50-65%) — Recovery & base building
Aerobic (65-80%) — Endurance & fat burning
Threshold (80-90%) — Lactate tolerance
Anaerobic (90-100%) — Peak speed & power
Set your max HR accurately for the most reliable zone calculations. The 220-minus-age formula is a rough starting point.
Running Coach — AI-Powered Advice
The Running Coach analyses your last 7 days of activity to generate a personalised daily recommendation — whether that's a rest day, an easy run, or a tempo session.

It also monitors your recovery status based on recent effort load, shows a 4-week training load chart, and can generate full training plans tailored to your level (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced).
The coach factors in race proximity — it automatically suggests taper and shakeout runs during race week.
Pace Calculator — Splits & Conversions
Enter a target time or pace and get instant split tables for standard race distances (5K, 10K, Half Marathon, Marathon). The calculator shows per-km and per-mile splits side by side.

It also converts between min/km and min/mile, and estimates equivalent race times using the Riegel formula so you can plan pacing strategies for any distance.
Use negative splits (running the second half slightly faster) for optimal race-day performance.
VO2 Max Lab — Your Fitness Score
VO2 Max measures the maximum volume of oxygen your body can use during intense exercise — the gold standard of aerobic fitness.

The lab estimates your VO2 Max from your best race performances using the Jack Daniels formula. Your score maps to a fitness category from Poor to Elite with age and gender adjustments. Track it over time to see your fitness trajectory.
VO2
Consistently training at 80-90% of max HR is the most effective way to raise your VO2 Max over time.
Badges — Unlock Achievements
Earn medals and badges for hitting milestones in your fitness journey. Achievements include total distance goals, activity streaks, race completions, and consistency targets.

Locked badges show their requirements so you always know what to aim for. Newly unlocked badges trigger a celebration toast — collect them all to complete your trophy wall!
Check the Achievements section regularly — some badges have hidden criteria that reward long-term consistency.
My Friends — Social & Leaderboard
Add friends to compare weekly and monthly stats on a shared leaderboard. See who's logging the most distance, maintaining the longest streak, or crushing the most challenges.

The social feed shows recent activity from your friends so you can cheer each other on. A little friendly competition goes a long way for motivation!
Invite training partners by sharing your profile link — accountability partners boost consistency by up to 65%.
